record.original_question: Is it decidable whether a given PCP instance has the unique-equality-continuation property?

evidence.quote: Is it decidable whether or not an instance of PCP satis- ﬁes the property of unique equality continuation instances?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the free monoid of words over $\Sigma$. An instance of the Post Correspondence Problem (PCP) is a finite list $I=((u_1,v_1),\dots,(u_n,v_n))$ of pairs of words $u_i,v_i\in\Sigma^*$. For a finite index sequence $\sigma=i_1i_2\cdots i_k\in\{1,\dots,n\}^*$ write $u_\sigma=u_{i_1}u_{i_2}\cdots u_{i_k}$ and $v_\sigma=v_{i_1}v_{i_2}\cdots v_{i_k}$. The sequence $\sigma$ is called admissible (an "equality continuation" candidate) if $u_\sigma$ is a prefix of $v_\sigma$ or $v_\sigma$ is a prefix of $u_\sigma$.

Say that the instance $I$ has the unique-equality-continuation property if for every admissible sequence $\sigma$ (including the empty sequence) there is at most one index $j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ such that the extended sequence $\sigma j$ is also admissible.

Decide: Is there an algorithm that, given an arbitrary PCP instance $I$ as input, determines whether $I$ has the unique-equality-continuation property?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up related results showing that PCP instances satisfying a uniqueness-of-continuation condition form a known decidable subclass (Halava–Harju–Karhumäki–Latteux, 2007, on instances with unique blocks; and the infinite PCP being decidable for unique-continuation instances), but no source was found that resolves the meta-question of whether the property of having unique equality continuation is itself decidable. The status therefore appears unresolved in publicly available sources.

status_evidence.title: Extension of the decidability of the marked PCP to instances with unique blocks
status_evidence.snippet: It is decidable whether an instance satisfying the uniqueness condition for continuations has an infinite solution; PCP is decidable for instances with unique blocks.
status_evidence.claim: Related decidability results for unique-continuation-type PCP subclasses are known, but they address the membership/solution problem on such instances rather than the recognition of the property itself.

status_evidence.title: Decidable Instances of the Post Correspondence Problem (Ackerman)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of decidable PCP subclasses including marked and unique-block instances.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys decidable PCP subclasses; does not establish decidability of recognizing the unique-equality-continuation property.
